trigger.summary: The current release still ships unsafe MCP defaults and relies on a Windows/MSYS update path that real downstream canaries had to bypass.
trigger.root_cause: Standalone template security, downstream drift promotion, and cross-platform update orchestration were validated as separate concerns, so downstream hardening never became the template SOT and helper safety never became a supported native workflow.

posture_evidence.summary: v4.9.5 is a public stable release consumed by PersonalAssistant and other dirty downstream repositories.
posture_evidence.ref: GitHub Release v4.9.5 and tasks/current.md release evidence

product.user_victory: A downstream operator can install and update the template on Windows or Linux without expanding code access, executing prompt-controlled shell text, exposing secrets, or using a manual helper workaround.
product.final_path: One exact release payload, one cross-platform sync engine, project-root MCP defaults, safe atomic configuration writers, and runtime security checks before publication.
product.falsifier: Any default MCP starts above the project root, shell metacharacters execute, a config symlink or secret backup is written, Windows needs manual helper calls, or a repeated sync is not a no-op.

change.summary: Promote proven downstream MCP hardening to the template SOT and replace Bash-owned sync orchestration with one Node engine behind compatible entrypoints.
change.scope: MCP defaults, context-router process and filesystem boundaries, bootstrap configuration writes and optional services, tool health resolution, sync orchestration, release provenance, documentation, and regression tests.

options.summary: Patch the four known MCP defects, retain Bash as the Windows canonical updater, and document preview-first recovery.

evidence.summary: The existing Bash path can apply clean fixtures on Linux and some Windows runs.

data_safety.reason: Git-for-Windows MSYS failures interrupt one non-transactional orchestration path and have required manual helper recovery.

evidence.summary: The known MCP defects can be repaired independently.
Existing CLI flags can remain unchanged.

verification.reason: A green Bash fixture does not eliminate the observed Windows fork/MSYS failure class.

rollback_recovery.reason: The current backup tag path can fail silently while reporting success.

product_outcome.basis: Windows operators still need a fragile shell environment and manual fallback.

correctness.basis: Known MCP defaults are fixed, but orchestration parity is not.

maintainability.basis: State transitions remain split across Bash inline Node and helper modules.

security.basis: Known prompt-input and root-scope defects are removed.

total_cost.basis: Low initial migration cost preserves the recurring Windows and duplicate-owner cost.

public_api.contract_diff: The existing sync CLI and manifest format remain unchanged; Bash continues to own orchestration.
public_api.consumer_tests: Existing Linux and Git-Bash smoke plus exact-tag downstream fixtures.
public_api.versioning: Patch release with immutable old tags.
public_api.semantic_checks: Help output, manifest schema, conflict behavior, and same-tag idempotence.

external_dependency.pinned_version: Node.js 20+, Git, Git Bash on Windows, and catalog-pinned MCP/tool versions.
external_dependency.compatibility: Keeps the currently documented Bash-first environment contract.
external_dependency.failure_behavior: MSYS/fork failures remain fail-stop and may require manual helper recovery.
external_dependency.integration_evidence: Existing CI and prior downstream migrations show both successes and real Windows orchestration failure.

options.summary: Move the sync state machine into one Node engine, keep Bash as a thin compatibility adapter, and repair the MCP/bootstrap/release trust boundaries in the same patch line.

evidence.summary: Existing Node safe-copy and manifest helpers already implement the critical atomic primitives used by successful native downstream recovery.
The engine preserves project ownership, conflict sidecars, dirty worktrees, and conflict-gated version advancement.
Project-root validation, argv-only child processes, reparse-safe writers, and explicit mutation opt-in directly close each P1 path.
The shell command remains available as an adapter and manifest/config formats stay unchanged.
evidence.ref: planned compatibility wrapper and existing formats

evidence.summary: Linux and native Windows can run the same engine with deterministic fixtures and exact-tag canaries.
Exact backup creation becomes fail-closed and the old public tags remain immutable rollback points.

product_outcome.basis: Operators no longer need a manual Windows helper workaround and receive safe defaults.
product_outcome.result: One supported native workflow and one payload SOT.
product_outcome.ref: Studio migration and current source diff

business_outcome.basis: Promoting recurring downstream fixes removes repeated incident and support work.
business_outcome.result: The release gate checks standalone defaults.

correctness.basis: One engine owns update decisions on both platforms.
correctness.baseline: Bash plus inline Node plus manual helper transition.

maintainability.baseline: 866-line shell state machine plus Node helpers.

reliability.basis: The native path removes the observed MSYS fork dependency.
reliability.baseline: MSYS apply failed in real downstream work.
reliability.result: Node process/file APIs on both platforms.

performance.basis: No speed claim is required; correctness and portability own the decision.

security.basis: Shell-free argv and fail-closed path boundaries remove known command/path injection classes.
security.baseline: Prompt-controlled shell strings and unguarded config writes.
security.result: No shell interpretation and atomic safe writers.
security.ref: Node child_process and filesystem boundary contract

transition_cost.basis: Porting and parity verification require more one-time work.

reversibility.basis: The compatibility adapter and immutable old tags preserve rollback while the engine is canaried.

total_cost.basis: Higher one-time port cost removes duplicate ownership, MSYS recovery, and repeated downstream hardening.

public_api.contract_diff: Manifest v1 and current sync flags remain supported; Node becomes canonical and Bash delegates without owning behavior.
public_api.consumer_tests: Native PowerShell/CMD and Linux calls plus Bash-shim plan parity and downstream exact-tag canaries.
public_api.versioning: Patch release preserves CLI compatibility and records Node as the canonical engine.
public_api.deprecation: The old Bash state machine is removed only after adapter parity passes; no public command is removed.
public_api.semantic_checks: Deterministic plan digest, zero-write conflict preflight, rollback injection, manifest schema, and same-tag no-op.

external_dependency.pinned_version: Node.js 20+ and Git remain required; MCP, n8n if retained, archive assets, and GitHub Actions use exact versions or digests.
external_dependency.compatibility: Node is already a required template dependency on Linux and Windows; Bash remains optional compatibility transport.
external_dependency.failure_behavior: Missing Node or Git fails before project mutation; unavailable optional tools remain disabled and do not weaken security defaults.
external_dependency.integration_evidence: Existing Node safety helpers passed Windows/Linux release fixtures and real downstream recovery; the new engine must pass the complete parity matrix.

cleanup.removal_condition: The old Bash state machine is removed in the same patch after Linux, native Windows, and downstream parity pass; only the adapter remains.
cleanup.absence_check: The Bash entrypoint contains argument forwarding only; security scans find no shell-owned copy, manifest, backup, or conflict transitions.

recommendation.reason: It removes both the unsafe payload and the recurring Windows recovery class while preserving public formats and a compatible shell entrypoint.
recommendation.rejected_alternative: Repairing only the defaults leaves the already-observed MSYS and duplicate-state-machine failures as an operating requirement.

envelope.outcome: Audit and bring the MCP, sync, and release path to production safety, then publish a corrected patch release.
envelope.scope: Template source MCP defaults, context-router, bootstrap, tool health, sync engine and adapters, release trust gates, documentation, tests, and isolated downstream canaries.
envelope.risk_limit: HIGH production template risk; no weakening of path, secret, ownership, or release provenance checks.
envelope.downtime_limit: No downstream service downtime and no fleet-wide apply.
envelope.cost_limit: Use existing local and open-source tooling; add no paid service.
envelope.release_limit: Publish a new immutable patch only after local and GitHub Linux/Windows gates pass; never mutate v4.9.5.
envelope.environment_limit: Template source, temporary fixtures, isolated CI runners, and reviewed canary copies; do not rewrite unrelated downstream product work.
envelope.rollback_requirement: Preserve public CLI/manifest compatibility, immutable old tags, fail-closed backup evidence, and repeatable same-tag no-op.
